content.text:
Fixed in `lib/request.js:48`.

## Root cause

The GHSA-444r-cwp2-x5xf hardening (`4e1db5bd`, shipped in 5.8.3) added an `a != null` guard to the hop-count trust function:

```js
return function (a, i) { return a != null && i < tp }
```

Under IIS/iisnode, Node is reached over a **named pipe**, so `socket.remoteAddress` is `undefined`. `@fastify/proxy-addr` builds the address chain as `[socket.remoteAddress, ...reversed XFF]` and truncates it at the first untrusted hop. With the new guard, hop 0 (`undefined`) was never trusted, so the chain was truncated to `[undefined]` and `req.ip` — the last entry — became `undefined`. The same applied to unix-socket deployments.

Verified with a socket lacking `remoteAddress`, before the fix:

```
trustProxy= 1  => ip: undefined  ips: [ undefined ]
```

## Fix

The address check doesn't belong in the numeric form: `trustProxy: <n>` means "trust `n` hops" and is address-agnostic by definition, so the guard was both incorrect and the source of the regression.

```js
if (typeof tp === 'number') {
  // Support trusting hop count.
  // The address is deliberately not checked here: ...
  return function (a, i) { return i < tp }
}
```

After the fix: `ip: 1.1.1.1`, `host`/`protocol` honor `x-forwarded-host`/`-proto` again for hop-count configs.

The address-based forms (string / array / CIDR / `'loopback'`) keep their `a != null` guard — and it is in fact redundant there, since `proxyAddr.compile(...)` already returns `false` for `undefined`, `null`, `''`, and non-IP values (I confirmed this against the installed `@fastify/proxy-addr`), so a pipe connection still gets no trust under those configs. That preserves the security fix: spoofed `x-forwarded-*` from an untrusted peer remains ignored wherever trust is address-based. With `trustProxy: <n>` the immediate peer is unconditionally trusted by design — which was already true of `req.ip` before the CVE fix — so nothing that the numeric form protected has changed.

## Tests

Added a regression test in `test/internals/request.test.js:290` covering a socket with no `remoteAddress` under `trustProxy: 1`. Full `test/internals/*.test.js` suite passes (362 tests), as do `test/trust-proxy.test.js` and `test/request-header-host.test.js` — including the two GHSA spoofing tests added by the original fix. I did not run eslint (the command needed approval); the change is a one-line edit plus a test in the surrounding style. Nothing committed.
